Just five days after winning our Endurance Cup as first man home in the "Southern", Royal Marine Tim Watson won his first Royal Navy CC Championship.

Jonathan Blackledge had been feeling “low” since the 4k World Cross Trial seven days earlier (he was second reserve for Fukuoka) but in spite of a week off, he also ran to a best ever time, chased by Tim Watson - back from a few weeks in South Africa.

In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).

With a 1:41 advantage Tim Watson smoothly ran our third sub-25 long lap - his fastest ever. A period of training in South Africa has done our Royal Marine bandsman a power of good and a challenge from Newham's Kairn Stone had little effect.

Karl O'Connell, the man due to start off the Bs was at first drafted in to take Paul Freary's place but the need not to bring in a reserve until we knew the decision had gone against us changed that plan, and with a minimum warm-up, A-team member Tim Watson came forward a leg.
